title: Safety Under Translated Actions
statement: Let $\Gamma$ and $S$ be types, let $k$ be a natural number, let $x$ be a word over the folded alphabet, and let $c$ be a configuration with $k$ work tapes over that alphabet and control states of the form specified by the safety invariant. If $c$ satisfies the safety invariant, then for every assignment of fold sides to the work tapes and every action over $\Gamma$ with state set $S$, applying the translated action using those sides and the symbols currently under the heads of $c$ produces a configuration satisfying the safety invariant.
hypotheses_covered: x is a list of folded-alphabet symbols
c is a configuration with the indicated folded alphabet and state type
a side is assigned to each work tape
a is an action over Γ with state set S
replaced:
Let $c$ be a configuration of a $k$-work-tape machine over the folded alphabet, on
an arbitrary folded-alphabet input, satisfying the safety invariant (control not in
the fresh initial state, nonnegative heads, correct origin flags at all nonnegative
cells).  Then for every assignment of sides to the work tapes and every base-machine
action $a$, applying the translation of $a$ --- relative to those sides and the
cells under the heads of $c$ --- again yields a configuration satisfying the safety
invariant.
